title: Anthropic's Valuation Collapsed by $500B
content:
Anthropic investors are considering slashing the company’s valuation by $500bn (£379bn) after its latest accounts revealed slowing growth, according to a report.
Some investors who attended Anthropic’s investor day on Wednesday in San Francisco discussed a valuation of about $1.5tn, Reuters reported, a significant step down from the $2tn that had previously been expected for the November listing.
At that meeting, Anthropic announced revenue of nearly $17bn as it reportedly turned a profit last quarter.
But investors were reported to be disappointed by the tech giant’s slowing growth rate and the inflated costs of AI infrastructure.
Its $17bn revenues were reportedly up around 45pc compared to the $11.6bn recorded in the second quarter. However, that was a slowdown from 146pc growth recorded between the first and second quarters.
Investor jitters come amid broader concerns over the ballooning cost of financing AI and a tech sell-off that has swept Wall Street and Asian markets in recent days.

report.summary: Anthropic investors weigh cutting its IPO valuation by $500bn to about $1.5tn after slowing growth and rising AI infrastructure costs.
report.background: Anthropic, founded in 2021 by former OpenAI executives, has become one of the most valuable AI labs behind the Claude family of models. Its investors had reportedly expected a November IPO at a $2tn valuation, reflecting the broader AI boom and intense demand for frontier models. But the company's latest investor day revealed revenue of nearly $17bn and a quarterly profit, alongside sharply slowing growth: quarter-over-quarter expansion fell from 146% to about 45%. At the same time, AI infrastructure costs—chips, data centers, energy—remain enormous. With Wall Street and Asian markets selling off tech stocks amid fears that AI spending is outpacing returns, Anthropic's IPO expectations are being repriced, testing whether private AI valuations can hold in a more skeptical market.
key_points: Investors at Anthropic’s San Francisco investor day discussed valuing the company at about $1.5tn, down from the $2tn previously expected for its November IPO. The reported $500bn cut reflects disappointment over slowing growth and the rising cost of AI infrastructure, marking a sharp reset for one of the sector’s most anticipated listings.

Anthropic disclosed nearly $17bn in revenue and reportedly turned a profit last quarter. However, revenue growth decelerated to roughly 45% quarter-on-quarter from 146% in the prior period. That slowdown, despite profitability, raised concerns that the company’s expansion is cooling faster than investors had priced in.

The valuation debate is unfolding amid a broad tech sell-off on Wall Street and in Asian markets. Investors are increasingly worried about the ballooning cost of financing AI data centers, chips, and energy, and whether AI companies can generate enough revenue to justify their massive capital expenditures.

If the lower valuation holds, it could reshape expectations for other AI IPOs and private fundraising rounds. Anthropic’s IPO was seen as a bellwether for the sector; a reduced listing could pressure rivals like OpenAI and signal that public markets will demand clearer paths to sustainable profit.
report.impact: For the AI industry, a reduced Anthropic valuation would signal a shift from growth-at-any-cost to disciplined economics. Rivals may face lower private valuations or tougher funding terms, especially for compute-heavy startups. Developers could see less subsidized API pricing, more emphasis on efficient models, and stronger interest in open-source and smaller models. Regular users may encounter fewer free-tier giveaways or higher prices, but also more reliable, cost-optimized products. The IPO outcome will test whether public investors accept AI’s long-term promise despite near-term infrastructure costs. It may also accelerate consolidation and partnerships as labs seek cheaper compute and diversified revenue.
report.tools: To follow the story, watch Anthropic’s Claude models and API, OpenAI’s platform, and Google Gemini for pricing and capability shifts. For open-source alternatives, track Meta Llama, Mistral, and serving tools like vLLM, Ollama, and Hugging Face. Reuters, the Telegraph, and SEC IPO filings will provide valuation updates. These resources help gauge whether AI usage and revenue can justify current infrastructure spending.
